target.title: Fix Claude never-prompt no-UI Keychain repair for missing credentials file (#1975)
target.body:
Fixes #1975.

## Summary

With the Claude provider's **Avoid Keychain prompts** setting (`claudeOAuthKeychainPromptMode = .never`), `shouldAllowClaudeCodeKeychainAccess` refused **all** `Claude Code-credentials` Keychain access unconditionally — including guaranteed no-UI reads (`KeychainNoUIQuery`, i.e. `kSecUseAuthenticationUI = .fail`). So when `~/.claude/.credentials.json` goes missing after a Claude account switch, the existing no-prompt repair path (`repairFromClaudeKeychainWithoutPromptIfAllowed`) was blocked before it could read a still-valid Keychain token, and the provider surfaced **"Claude OAuth credentials not found. Run `claude` to authenticate."** even though a healthy token was sitting in the Keychain.

## The design decision (the one thing to sign off)

`.never` now means **"no interactive prompts"**, not **"no Keychain access at all."** The gate gains an explicit `allowKeychainPrompt` flag:

```swift
case .never:
    // A guaranteed no-UI read (KeychainNoUIQuery) must still repair a missing
    // credentials file from a valid Keychain item without ever surfacing a prompt.
    return !allowKeychainPrompt
```

- Guaranteed-non-interactive call sites (missing-file repair, freshness sync, fingerprint/candidate probes, preflight-only checks) pass `allowKeychainPrompt: false` → permitted under `.never`, and every one of them reads through `KeychainNoUIQuery`, which fails closed rather than prompting.
- The interactive readers (`loadFromClaudeKeychain`, `loadFromClaudeKeychainWithPromptIfAllowed`) keep the default `true` → still fully blocked under `.never`.
- The **Advanced → Disable Keychain access** kill switch (`keychainAccessAllowed`) is checked before the mode switch and still hard-blocks everything, unchanged.

Net effect: `.never` keeps its promise (no UI ever) while no longer failing closed when only the Keychain — not the file — holds the credential.

## Intentionally unchanged

- **The experimental `security(1)` CLI reader is untouched.** It deliberately ignores prompt policy today (see `experimental reader ignores prompt policy and cooldown for background silent check`), and under the default `securityFramework` strategy it is inert (`shouldPreferSecurityCLIKeychainRead` requires the experimental strategy). This PR does not route any new caller through that subprocess — details in the review thread below.
- `shouldAttemptFreshnessSyncFromClaudeKeychain` / owner-resolution keep their explicit `.never` early-outs (#2011 deliberately minimized background Keychain IO under `.never`).
- CodexBar-owned OAuth cache gating under `.never` (#2011) — untouched; its zero-IO regression tests still pass.

## Verification

- [x] `swift build` (all targets)
- [x] `swift test --filter ClaudeOAuthCredentialsStoreNeverPromptKeychainRepairTests` (3 tests, macOS-guarded)
- [x] The repair test **fails on `main`** with `ClaudeOAuthCredentialsError.notFound` — the reporter's exact error — and passes with this change (before/after below)
- [x] `swift test --filter Claude` and the full `ClaudeOAuthCredentialsStoreSecurityCLITests` suite green (no regression to the experimental reader)
- [x] `swiftformat --lint` + `swiftlint --strict` clean; suite guarded by `#if os(macOS)` so the Linux SwiftPM job stays green

Tests use the existing synthetic Keychain override hooks (`withClaudeKeychainOverridesForTesting`, `ClaudeKeychainOverrideStore`) + per-test isolated cache stores — no live Keychain access or prompts, per `AGENTS.md`.

## Before / after (deterministic, same fixture)

Same isolated fixture — missing credentials file, valid synthetic `Claude Code-credentials` payload, `.never`, background:

```
# on main (pre-fix):
✘ never mode repairs a missing credentials file … : Caught error: .notFound   ← the #1975 symptom

# with this change:
info … Claude keychain credentials loaded without prompt; syncing OAuth cache
✔ never mode repairs a missing credentials file …                             ← source=.claudeKeychain, owner=.claudeCLI, no prompt
```

## On the "real behavior proof" request

Happy to provide more if it helps. One transparency note so I'm not overclaiming: a live end-to-end capture on a real account requires a **Keychain-ACL-trusted (signed) build** reading the real `Claude Code-credentials` item — the item's ACL is keyed to the signing identity, so an unsigned local build can't read it under the no-UI policy, and I don't want to fabricate a capture. The change is a pure *fail-closed → no-UI-recover* logic change, and the test above pins it deterministically (fails pre-fix with the exact reported error, passes post-fix, no UI). If you'd like, I can add a `Scripts/repro_keychain_*.sh` in the style of #2011 that stands up the missing-file + Keychain scenario for a signed build to exercise — just say the word.
